# Week 8 Robot showcase

> [Download the Word version](W08_showcase_Speaker_Notes.docx) · This Markdown copy is generated from the DOCX. Update the DOCX, then run `python scripts/sync_documents.py --write` from the repository root. Print layout, page breaks, headers/footers, and writing-space height remain in Word.

Speaker notes for the one-hour showcase using the saved Week 7 projects.

### Class preparation

**Print and bring**  Use the Week 8 showcase packet. If both Week 7 courses are intact, print pages 1–2 and 35–58 on Letter at Actual Size, single-sided, with automatic orientation. Bring both courses, two stopwatches, a slot timer, saved exhibits, cubes and Week 7 trial records.

**Set the floor**  Tape both 50 × 160 cm courses flat. Check START on row A and FINISH on D, 60 cm apart, with 90 cm of printed runout and clear floor beyond. Leave the fixed tape mark where the timekeeper can see it. If rebuilding, match the tile ticks and check the 5 cm ruler.

**Queue the four projects**  Retrieve the actual saved SPIKE projects and an offline backup. T1/T2 normally share Kit A and T3/T4 share Kit B. Check the correct hub, A left, B right and Stop. Rehearse every team’s configuration on its original kit with its calibrated travel, approved speed, same tray and same cube. Choose a Week 7 configuration with three valid runs.

**Roles and backup**  Assign two robot mentors, two build mentors and one timekeeper per lane. Confirm visitors with staff. If the selected setup fails rehearsal, retest the team’s last verified timed setup on its original kit and lane. If motion is unavailable, keep the demo slot and show the saved code, cradle and Week 7 evidence.

## Slide 1 Robot showcase

**0–7 minutes**  Hand out the individual check before coaching. Read a question aloud if needed without supplying an answer. The four items review sequence, wheel travel, loops and the Week 5 marker rule. Use the mentor guide key after collection.

**7–12 minutes**  Brief students on their tested setup and three speaking parts. Ask each team to show one decision and one real observation. Visitors stand outside both courses and their runout areas.

## Slide 2 Reuse the Week 7 course and program

**Before class**  Tape both courses flat and verify the measured distance and clear runout. Reopen each team’s saved project in SPIKE and select its tested kit. Verify that the travel value, chosen speed and attachment match the trial sheet. Test the loaded configuration and Stop on the actual floor.

**Show the start**  Seat the cube, line up the fixed side mark with START and point toward FINISH. The robot needs room at both ends. An attachment edge may extend past the mark.

**Check the program**  Have a child point to the speed passed to sprint(speed) or another choice in the saved timed delivery program. Keep the tested settings for the live demonstration.

## Slide 3 Rehearse the run and the timing

**12–24 minutes**  T1/T3 rehearse from 12–18 while T2/T4 finish exhibits. Swap from 18–24. Rotate driver, navigator and observer every two minutes. The driver starts after “clear.” The navigator resets the stopped robot. The observer records what happened.

**Timekeeper**  Wait through R and the one-second pause. Press START at the first physical movement. Press STOP as the same chassis mark crosses FINISH. Record tenths. Watch until the robot has fully stopped. It must keep its cube, stay in the lane and stop in the runout.

**Record the outcome**  Write DNF if the mark never crosses. If it crosses and the run fails a condition, record the time and mark the delivery invalid. At 24–28, queue the four projects and position the first team.

## Slide 4 Your four-minute showcase

**28–44 minutes**  T1 starts at 28, T2 at 32, T3 at 36 and T4 at 40. This slide shows elapsed time within each slot. The lead calls the transitions and holds the four-minute boundary.

**0:00–0:45  Explain**  Give each child one short part. Child one names the user and delivery job. Child two points to one program choice. Child three shows a cradle or build change and tells what an earlier test showed.

**0:45–2:00  Run and report**  Confirm lane clear. The driver starts. The mentor times the crossing and checks the full stop. The observer reports what happened. If the demo fails or cannot start, explain the observed issue, show the recorded trial evidence and name a next test.

**2:00–3:00  Answer**  Invite one audience question. If there is none, ask what the team held fixed or how its build helped.

**3:00–4:00  Reset**  After motion ends, collect the cube, clear the lane, save the result and hand over. The next team confirms its project and kit before anyone presses Run.

## Slide 5 Show the evidence you collected

**During demos, then 44–50 minutes**  Invite each team to show a time, a count of valid runs or a brief observation from its build. Use a mean time only for a Week 7 set with three valid runs. Keep failed attempts in the record.

**Example prompt**  Ask what changed, what stayed fixed and what the actual run showed. If a live run fails, compare it with an earlier verified result and propose one specific test. Use the same slot even if the team needs to demonstrate with code and a stationary model.

## Slide 6 What we learned and what comes next

**50–54 minutes**  Run two short conversations in parallel. Give each child time to point out one thing they learned or one observation from another team. Accept pointing, a brief oral answer or a demonstration.

**54–60 minutes**  Save four final projects, label and store the builds, stop and charge both hubs, collect sheets and follow YMCA pickup procedures. Keep completed student records private. Record observed hardware problems and outcomes in SESSION\_PREP.md.
